A modest 7.5% chance for 34°C accounts for minor upside potential if boundary-layer mixing or insolation exceeds expectations, while probabilities drop sharply outside 31–34°C. With resolution imminent and no incoming weather systems indicated, the market reflects the current stable atmospheric setup favoring these two outcomes.

Official guidance from regional agencies anticipates continued warm advection with only modest cooling from scattered showers, keeping maximum temperatures well above the 26°C threshold. Only an anomalous, unmodeled cold surge—rare in late August—would alter this market-implied outcome.

Recent model runs highlight a transient Atlantic front or upper-level trough increasing cloud cover and precipitation chances, which historically suppresses peak temperatures by 2–4 °C relative to clear-sky climatology for late August (long-term average highs near 22–23 °C). 

Wind direction (southwesterly to westerly, 7–10 mph) and surface moisture from overnight lows in the low teens °C further limit boundary-layer heating. Traders therefore assign the highest implied probabilities to the narrow 20–22 °C band, reflecting both the consensus forecast and residual uncertainty over exact shower timing and any late-day clearing that could allow a brief spike toward 23 °C. Updated NWP guidance and radar trends through the evening of August 21 will be the key near-term catalysts.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from the Servicio Meteorológico Nacional and numerical models indicate a polar air mass will dominate over Buenos Aires on August 22, with clear skies and westerly winds limiting daytime heating and supporting radiative cooling overnight. Trader consensus reflected in the 51.5 % implied probability on 14 °C and secondary support for 15 °C and 13 °C appears to incorporate model spread and the potential for modest warming if winds weaken or insolation increases slightly beyond baseline expectations. Upcoming official updates from SMN and refined short-range model runs will likely refine these probabilities ahead of resolution.
